Both, but for different jobs: the weights on your three gym days keep and build muscle while you're eating below maintenance, and steps or cardio add to the burn. The fat loss itself comes mostly from staying near 1800 kcal. If you only had time for one, keep the lifting and walk more.
Nice. Roughly how long did the 50 rounds take?

Do 4 rounds with a minute's rest between: 15 squats, 10 push-ups (knees if needed), 10 lunges each leg, 30 seconds of plank and 20 jumping jacks. That's about 20 minutes and works the whole body. Tell me when it's done and I'll count it for today.

Soreness two days after squats is normal, it usually peaks around now. Go anyway and train upper body, or do a lighter session with an easy walk; moving helps it ease. If it's a sharp or one-sided pain rather than a general ache, rest it.
Nothing today: every check is met, 1710 kcal, 124 g protein, 9100 steps and your pull day done. That's 6 of the last 7 days on track, so keep doing exactly this.

That happens to everyone, and it usually passes faster if you don't wait for it. For today just do one thing: a 15-minute walk, or log your next meal. Is something in particular weighing on you?

Great start: you've logged every day so far, which is the habit everything else builds on. Weight's already 81.9 kg from 84.2. Keep logging this week and we'll start fine-tuning next week.

Yes, it can: PCOS doesn't stop fat loss, though it can make it slower, so please keep your gynaecologist or endocrinologist in the loop, especially about any medication. What helps most is what the plan already does: a steady deficit at 1500 kcal, protein near 95 g, and strength training three days a week, which improves insulin sensitivity.

Check that with your doctor or pharmacist, since thyroxine timing matters. Usually it's taken on an empty stomach with water, and tea, coffee or milk are kept 30 to 60 minutes after, but follow what they've told you.

A fasting sugar of 180 needs a doctor soon, so please get it checked before choosing a diet. Meanwhile keep logging, keep your meals balanced with protein and fibre at each one, and keep walking after meals; that's safe either way.

I'd skip them: most fat burners are mainly caffeine and other stimulants, the effect is tiny, and they can cause palpitations, anxiety and poor sleep. Your 0.55 kg a week is a solid pace without them.
Magnus is built for adults, so I can't coach you on supplements at 17. Please talk to a doctor or your parents about creatine and whey; food and sleep do most of the work at your age anyway.

I'm glad you feel in control, but 600 kcal is too little, well under the 1200 I'd ever suggest, and it tends to backfire with hunger, low energy and muscle loss. You still have room for a proper dinner tonight. How are you feeling?

Please stop running and get that checked by a doctor today; chest pain with dizziness during exercise needs medical attention. If it comes back, or you feel it at rest, go to an emergency room right away.

Dizziness is your body telling you it's not getting enough, so please eat a proper meal now and go back to regular meals. If it continues, see a doctor. You're already losing at a good pace, and speeding it up this way mostly costs muscle and energy.

If your doctor has you on 1000 kcal under supervision, follow their plan. I can't set a target below 1200 kcal in the app, though, so I'll leave yours at 1800 and you can follow the doctor's numbers directly. Want me to keep logging meals as usual?

Have a good sargi before sunrise: something with protein and slow carbs like paneer paratha with curd, fruit, and plenty of water or coconut water. Take it easy during the day and skip any workout, then break the fast gently with water and a light, normal dinner rather than a big feast. If you have any medical condition, check with your doctor about fasting without water.
